name: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
explanation: BFS traverses a graph level-by-level using a Queue (FIFO), guaranteeing shortest path discovery in unweighted graphs.
learning_objectives: Utilize a Queue to explore graph nodes level by level
Maintain a visited set to avoid infinite cycles in graph traversal
Track path distance accurately level by level
common_misconceptions: Using a Stack instead of a Queue (converting BFS to DFS)
Marking nodes as visited when dequeued instead of when enqueued (causing duplicate processing)

no_hint.message: Your queue-based level traversal logic looks great. Keep tracking visited nodes.
no_hint.next_step: Ensure nodes are added to the visited set immediately upon enqueueing.
no_hint.reflection_question: Why must a node be marked visited as soon as it enters the queue?

concept.message: Breadth-First Search explores all immediate neighbors of a node before moving deeper, using a FIFO Queue.
concept.next_step: Initialize a queue with your starting node and a set to track visited nodes.
concept.reflection_question: Why does BFS guarantee finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph?

guided.message: Pop the front node from the queue, inspect its unvisited neighbors, mark them visited, and enqueue them.
guided.next_step: Loop while the queue is non-empty.
guided.reflection_question: What data structure guarantees first-in-first-out node processing?

pseudocode.message:
queue = [start_node], visited = {start_node}
WHILE queue IS NOT EMPTY:
    node = queue.pop_left()
    FOR neighbor IN node.neighbors:
        IF neighbor NOT IN visited:
            visited.add(neighbor)
            queue.append(neighbor)
pseudocode.next_step: Write the BFS loop using a collections.deque in Python or Queue interface in Java/C++.
pseudocode.reflection_question: What happens if a neighbor is added to the queue without checking the visited set?

full_solution.message: BFS uses a Queue to process nodes level-by-level, ensuring O(V + E) traversal and shortest path guarantees in unweighted graphs.
full_solution.next_step: Test with disconnected graph components or graphs containing single nodes.
full_solution.reflection_question: How would you modify BFS to track the exact shortest path sequence instead of just the distance?

reflection_questions: How does the FIFO property of a Queue enforce level-by-level graph traversal?
Why is a visited set essential for cyclic graphs?
pseudocode:
queue = Queue(), visited = Set()
queue.enqueue(start), visited.add(start)
WHILE queue NOT EMPTY:
    curr = queue.dequeue()
    FOR nxt IN adj[curr]:
        IF nxt NOT IN visited:
            visited.add(nxt)
            queue.enqueue(nxt)

complexity.time: O(V + E) - Visits every vertex V and edge E once
complexity.space: O(V) - Storage for queue and visited set
